title: Fixing Kubernetes CFS CPU Throttling Freezes
prompt: A latency-sensitive Java/Netty payment gateway running in Kubernetes (`requests.cpu: '500m'`, `limits.cpu: '2'`) on 64-vCPU nodes has a median latency of 4ms, but p99 latency spikes to 95-120ms every few seconds. Node CPU utilization is only 35%, yet `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total` is 45% and `nr_throttled` climbs rapidly. The JVM sees all 64 host cores via `/proc/cpuinfo` (or defaults) and spawns 64 Netty/ForkJoin/G1GC threads. Diagnose the Linux CFS bandwidth mechanism causing the 95ms freezes and fix the Kubernetes and runtime configuration.

spark.summary: With limits.cpu: 2 (200 ms quota per 100 ms period) on a 64-vCPU host, a JVM spawning 64 Netty/G1GC threads burns its 200 ms quota in 3.1 ms and freezes for 96.9 ms; capping ActiveProcessorCount=2 and removing limits.cpu (or using Static CPU Manager) drops p99 below 15 ms.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, never let a container spawn 64 threads inside a 2-vCPU cgroup quota, and avoid arbitrary limits.cpu on latency-sensitive pods (or use Guaranteed QoS with integer CPU + Static CPU Manager).

explanation.foundation: Production Kubernetes clusters eliminate CFS throttling using two proven strategies:
explanation.core:

```yaml
# Payment Gateway PodSpec: Align JVM threads & eliminate CFS quota freezes
containers:
  - name: payment-gateway
    env:
      - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS

        memory: "4Gi"

        memory: "4Gi"
```
